properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 by `tools/vocabulary_reach.py` over the committed export (2527 nodes, 10353 edges) and the committed toolsnaps. 215 declared node properties across 29 types; 176 parameter names across the served tools, with `create_node`/`create_edge` excluded.

  18  CANDIDATES        the type IS used, the property NEVER is, and no typed tool accepts the name
  10  UNUSED BUT OFFERED  zero uses but a tool does accept it — probably unused rather than unreachable
  46  SAYS NOTHING      the node type has NO instances, so a zero on its properties is vacuous
  42  EDGE VOCABULARY   edge types with no edges, or properties never set on edges that do exist

⭐ THE STANDOUT, AND IT LANDS ON A REQUIREMENT ACCEPTED THE SAME DAY: `Capability.inputs`, `Capability.outputs` and `Capability.capability_type` are 0 OF 170. Spot-checked in the source rather than inferred — `add_capability` sets only name, description and status, and NOTHING anywhere in either crate writes those three. A capability's functional signature, what goes in and what comes out, is declared vocabulary that has never once been recorded. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` (accepted 2026-08-18) says every element is a black box with INNER FUNCTION AND INTERFACES; at the capability tier those two properties ARE that interface, and they are empty.

OTHER CANDIDATES: `Fragment.{created_at,created_by,intent,phase,summary}` (0 of 168), `Project.mirror_*` (4, 0 of 1), `Artifact.{created_at,signature}` (0 of 190), `Snapshot.captured_at` (0 of 144), `Release.created_at` (0 of 36), `Question.prompt_id` (0 of 46). The timestamp cluster is its own theme: five separate `created_at`/`captured_at` fields, all declared, none ever set.

⭐ `DECOMPOSES` HAS ZERO EDGES, and `req:decomposition-covers-its-parent` is ACCEPTED. That is the same shape as SPECIFIES: an accepted requirement whose edge type exists and has never been drawn. Not repaired here.

THE INSTRUMENT WAS VALIDATED AGAINST WHAT WAS ALREADY KNOWN before its new findings were believed: it catches `SUPERSEDES` (zero edges, known), `GOVERNED_BY.ruling` (added 2026-08-17, 0 of 912, correctly reported as not yet used), and it stopped reporting `SPECIFIES` the moment the 44 edges were exported — dead-to-live in one run.

⚠️ WHAT THE NUMBER IS NOT. 18 is not a defect count and not a delete list. Three of the four known instances were WANTED and got a parameter; deletion would have been the wrong repair every time. Zero usage is evidence, not proof — a property can be writable and simply never needed, which is what the second bucket is for.
